source_title: Ella Stiller Reveals Which Family Member She Was the Most ‘Excited’ to Tell About ‘Cupertino’ - People.com
source_excerpt:
The actress tells PEOPLE why she had a “gut feeling” about landing her biggest TV role yet and which family member she couldn’t wait to tell
Julia Moore is a TV Writer-Reporter at PEOPLE. She has been working at PEOPLE since 2022.
Ella Stiller plays fearless legal assistant Christy Palladino in CBS’ new legal drama Cupertino
The 24-year-old tells PEOPLE why she had a “gut feeling” she’d land her biggest role yet and which family member she was most excited to tell
“I don’t have to do any work to get in character for her,” Ella says of Christy. “I feel like she lives inside of me and she always has”
Ella Stiller had a feeling she’d found the perfect role when she first read for Christy Palladino.
The oldest child of Ben Stiller and Christine Taylor , Ella, 24, landed what she calls the “biggest” role of her career yet on CBS’ new legal drama, Cupertino. She plays Christy, a fearless legal assistant who helps Michael (Mike Colter) and Olivia (Rachel Keller) launch their own law firm after they’re wrongfully fired by a startup.
“I read the script and I fell in love with Christy immediately,” Ella tells PEOPLE, recalling the “gut feeling” she had about landing the role. “I was like, it’s kind of a match made in heaven. I don’t give myself that pat on the back that often, but I read the role, and I thought, I don’t know that this is anyone else. I think she’s just me.”
Despite that certainty, there was a stressful, weeks-long period between her audition and the phone call that confirmed she’d secured the role. “I was carrying crystals around everywhere,” she recalls. “Then I got the call, and I was like, oh, thank God. Because I had a good feeling, but you never know — and it felt too good to be true.”
After getting the good news, Ella called her family, starting with her mom, Christine Taylor, who “freaked out.” But there was one person she was especially excited to tell: her grandmother. “The most exciting one was my grandma, my mom’s mom, because she lives for procedural television. She lives for CBS. She’s like — this is her whole life.”
“I thought, wow, this is for you, Grammy. I was really excited to tell her, and she loves the show. She’s obsessed.”
Ella learned she’d landed the role in January, and filming began two months later. Now, as production continues, “It’s been a wild, wild ride and I have loved every single second of it,” she says.
“Someone said recently to me, ‘It doesn’t feel like homework.’ It’s so relevant and so topical,” she says of the series, which follows Michael and Olivia as they represent clients who, like them, have been wronged by Silicon Valley’s elite. “I think [creators] Robert and Michelle [King] did a really great job of … centering the humans that are being affected.”
Though Christy isn’t a lawyer, Ella says her character brings a sense of “humanity” to the courtroom. “It’s very freeing to play her because she just says the stuff that everyone else is thinking — I love that. I love just being able to say it out loud and be fearless and be bold. I think that the only difference really between me and her is that she has a little bit more of a fearlessness thing. It’s freeing, and it’s made me want to live my life more like that.”
“She’s fierce and doesn’t take any bullshit, and that’s always been my whole thing. To get to really actively feel that and live in that power is really special,” Ella continues. “She’s always along for the ride. I think that’s another thing that is fun to live out through her — is just [being] a little bit more of a go-with-the-flow [type of person].”
Despite the qualities she hopes to learn from Christy, Ella says playing the character comes naturally. “I don’t have to do any work to get in character for her. I feel like she lives inside of me and she always has.”

Ella also credits her time on the third season of HBO’s The Comeback with helping prepare her for the demands of a larger role. Calling the HBO comedy “the greatest experience ever,” Ella says, “Being there and not having the stakes rest on me every day, to feel like I was living the life of what it is to be a series regular on a TV show without having the major responsibility that the scene is make-or-break because of what I do was really nice.”
“I just gave myself the freedom to be like — I’m never going to do anything that’s going to make it bad. I can only make it funnier, or I can only do something great that would be an added bonus,” she says of her approach to the Lisa Kudrow series. “That was a really amazing way to get more comfortable being on set, and I feel like then being able to come into [ Cupertino ] and know what that is [like], it totally all feels like the exact trajectory that I needed.”
New episodes of Cupertino air Thursdays at 10 p.m. ET on CBS and stream the next day on Paramount+.
